title: Use the tickets with a deadline
hook: Six tickets expire after this event. Which choice leaves fewer of them unused?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Choose among equivalent resources using a stated expiration deadline.

misconception: Equivalent resources have identical consequences regardless of deadline.
objective: Choose among equivalent resources using a stated expiration deadline.

claims.text: Six tickets expire at the event’s end. Six others remain valid later. Use four before the deadline. Scaled model; fictional tickets; equal acceptance; no food guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Used=4, A=2tickets and B=6tickets. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-",6,"x"]]; B=6; x denotes Used. At x=4, A=2, B=6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Using deadline tickets first reduces the expiring remainder. Using the other tickets leaves all six deadline tickets unused. This is a declared ticket-validity model, not guidance about food or unsafe expired goods.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-",6,"x"]]; B=6; x denotes Used. At x=4, A=2, B=6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Five tickets expire tonight; five others stay valid later. You use three tonight, choosing the expiring ones first. How many expiring tickets go unused? Correct: 2. Using the expiring tickets first leaves 5 − 3 = 2 to expire; using the others first would leave all 5.

recall.question: Five tickets expire tonight; five others stay valid later. You use three tonight, choosing the expiring ones first. How many expiring tickets go unused?
recall.why: Using the expiring tickets first leaves 5 − 3 = 2 to expire; using the others first would leave all 5.
